why: The printed line reads (12)^2 x 0.05 / 0.15 = 0.0048, which is self-refuting: (12)^2 x 0.05 / 0.15 = 48, not 0.0048. The value 0.0048 is what (0.12)^2 x 0.05 / 0.15 gives, and 0.12 is the alpha_1 the example itself defines two lines above as 12/100. So the base of the square has lost its decimal point. The printed final answer 6.93 % is correct.

Second, it prints "alpha_2 = 0.0693 %", but 0.0693 is the degree of dissociation, a fraction — the percentage is the 6.93 % printed on the very next line, so the stray per-cent sign made two consecutive lines disagree by a factor of 100.
